subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps (SDK + function calling)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@cloudfin.com>, Lily Ho <lily.ho@cloudfin.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps (SDK + function calling)

Hi Sam / Lily —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Great conversation — I think there’s a clear production use case for Redwood in your fraud-detection pipeline.

Key pain points you shared:
- High inference cost on current model serving for short, low-latency scoring (especially peak mornings).
- Inconsistent outputs across model versions; hard to pin regressions to model vs prompt changes.
- Need structured output (JSON) for downstream rule engine and a way to rerank candidate responses/embeddings for similarity checks.

Goals we heard:
1) Reduce per-inference cost by ~30% while keeping 99th pct latency under 120ms for single-turn scoring.
2) Get predictable rollouts and telemetry to detect quality regressions.
3) Integrate an embeddings + reranking flow for candidate retrieval and scoring.

Integration + product fit notes:
- SDK: We recommended the latest Redwood SDK (v2.4) which includes streaming + function-calling helpers. There are a couple minor client changes: the .streamResponses() helper and new structured_output schema parameter. I attached a one-pager with sample calls.
- Function calling: Useful for enforcing strict JSON outputs for your rule engine. We showed using function signature + required fields to guarantee type-safe outputs.
- Streaming: For batch scoring UX you can stream partial tokens; for single-turn scoring we'll use short sequences + batching to meet latency SLOs.
- Embeddings / Reranking: We suggested using our dense embeddings endpoint for candidate vectors and the reranking API for fine-grained scoring; runs as a two-step: retrieval by vector similarity -> rerank with model in embed+context mode.

Proposed next steps:
- Action: CloudFin to share a small sample dataset (anonymized) and expected scoring label format by Friday Nov 12. (Sam)
- Action: Redwood to send a Mutual Action Plan and SDK integration notes + sample function-calling templates (attached). (Marissa)
- Technical deep-dive: Schedule a 60-min session next week with your infra/ML engineer to walk SDK changes and latency tuning. (Rishi to lead)

Attachments: redwood_sdk_integration_notes.pdf, mutual_action_plan.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once Sam confirms availability.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few quick notes from our side:

- Confirming we can share an anonymized sample of 5k events (with labels) by EOD Friday. Will strip PII.
- For latency, our main SLA is 100ms p99 for single-item scoring during peak. If Redwood can meet that with the recommended batching profile we’re in good shape.
- On reranking — Lily will own the evaluation criteria; she prefers to see an initial A/B comparison using your reranking API and our current BM25 baseline.

Would like to schedule the deep-dive next Tue (Nov 16) 10:00–11:00 PT if that works for your team. I’ll add our infra lead (will include in follow-up).

Sam

Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps (SDK + function calling)

Hi Sam / Lily —

Thanks for confirming and for the dataset commitment. I’ll own the technical deep-dive next week. Preliminary notes so the infra team has context:

- Latency tuning: For your 100ms p99 target we’ll likely recommend: single-item hot paths using a CPU+GPU co-located pool (dedicated), sequence trimming to <64 tokens, and dynamic batching with max batch size 8 for peak windows.
- SDK changes: the client-side change is minimal — replace generate() with generate({structured_output: schema}) or use the function-calling wrapper. We’ll share code snippets in the session.
- Function calling: we’ll provide JSON schema templates that validate on the server side; if you prefer, Redwood can enforce strict schema and reject non-conforming outputs so your rule engine never sees malformed JSON.
- Embeddings/reranking: initial test plan: 1k retrieval candidates -> embed -> top-50 rerank with context window. Expect to run rerank on a smaller quantized model to reduce cost.

I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue Nov 16 10:00 PT and attach a short tech checklist for the call.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
